E3 demonstrates that a dual-phase alloy with preexisting Cr-rich precipitates avoids intergranular embrittlement and retains ductility at 600–700°C, supporting the precipitate-sink strategy and improved ductility. However, the cited evidence does not provide direct atom-probe measurements of Ni, Cr, Mn segregation or prove that precipitates absorb these specific elements; the mecha
premises: Fast nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, Mn to grain boundaries occurs in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi at 400–700°C
This GB segregation reduces cohesion and causes intergranular brittle fracture
Preexisting Cr-rich precipitates can absorb the embrittling species (Ni, Cr, Mn)
Absorbing embrittling species into precipitates preserves GB integrity and ductility
The engineered dual-phase alloy shows improved ductility/toughness over the single-phase baseline at intermediate temperatures
